name: Abyss
fit: Research, deep-dive essays, data storytelling, mysterious launches
keywords: deep sea ocean flashlight dark data story bioluminescent
idea: The page sits at the bottom of a deep-sea trench. It is almost pitch black; your cursor is the submersible's lamp, and only bioluminescent creatures glow on their own.
note: Live: move the pointer (or focus the stage and use the arrow keys) to sweep the lamp; the depth gauge tracks it. "Surface" lifts the darkness so everything can be read.
borrowed: Deep-sea exploration: submersible lamps cutting through black water, marine snow, bioluminescent jellyfish and anglerfish lures, depth gauges, specimen numbering from expedition logs, and the hush of the hadal zone.
mood: Mysterious, quiet, rewarding curiosity. Suits research write-ups, long-form deep dives, data stories that reveal one thing at a time, and teaser launch pages. The reveal is the content strategy.

type.meta: Display · Fraunces 300, italic for the one word that matters

motion: One overlay: `radial-gradient(circle 170px at var(--x) var(--y), transparent, …97% black)` driven by the pointer.
Creatures sit above the overlay so they glow in the dark; they bob (5.5s) and sway (3.2s) out of phase.
Marine snow drifts down forever on two offset layers; depth reads off the lamp's y position.
watchouts: Hidden text is inaccessible text. Always ship a "Surface" control and never hide navigation in the dark.
Touch has no hover: on phones, default the lamp to the content or start surfaced.
Keep it to one lamp-lit hero. A whole site in the dark is tiring.
